transaction(callable $mutator): mixedRun one whole-file transaction under an exclusive sidecar lock: re-read the on-disk bytes, hand this instance to $mutator, and publish iff the mutator changed anything. Concurrent control-plane processes therefore serialize on the lock — each one's mutator sees the OTHER's committed rows, which is what kills the lost-update window. The mutator's value is returned; an exception aborts without publishing and the lock still releases.
save(): voidPersist the whole store atomically with tight permissions: the file holds authentication material, so it is created 0600 and the directory 0700 (umask-independent — the mode is set on the temp inode BEFORE the payload lands, and rename carries it onto the target). Raw write of the current snapshot — concurrency-safe mutation goes through transaction() instead.

SugarCraft\GitServer\Git

GitDaemon final class

Real daemon-mode Git daemon: binds to a port and answers the git-upload-pack advertisement over the anonymous git:// transport. Each request delegates to a one-shot REAL git upload-pack --advertise-refs child, so the advertisement is byte-exact git output; completing the negotiation past the advertisement is a disclosed follow-up (a stateless-rpc relay per connection), and clients that send wants are closed after the flush — visibly, never as a corrupted half-transfer. The daemon is READ-ONLY by construction — the git protocol carries no authentication, so receive-pack (push) is refused outright and lives on the authenticated transports.

MethodSummary
__construct(Config $config)
setStats(Stats $stats): voidInject a stats collector (default: the shared Stats instance).
registerRepo(Repo $repo): void
registerRepos(iterable $repos): void
registerUser(User $user): void
setUsers(iterable $users): void
addSubscription(Subscription $subscription): voidRegister a subscription for cleanup on graceful shutdown.
clearSubscriptions(): voidUnregister all subscriptions (used after shutdown).
serve(string $pidFile = ''): intStart the daemon in blocking mode.
serveAsync(?LoopInterface $loop = null, string $pidFile = ''): PromiseInterfaceStart the daemon in async (event-loop) mode — the opt-in counterpart to the blocking serve(). Connections are accepted via Loop::addReadStream() on the listening socket and each client stream is registered with the loop, so request handling never blocks the loop waiting for readability. The per-request protocol work is the same synchronous delegation the blocking mode runs — a git upload-pack child driven through the bounded StdioPipe pump — executing inside the readiness callback, so a long transfer still delays the other clients on THIS transport for its duration. That is the git:// daemon's own serial contract, disclosed and standing (it is the shape git's reference daemon shipped too); the smart-HTTP front door took a different path with the owner-8b worker pool — each HTTP connection is served by its own forked worker (\SugarCraft\GitServer\HttpSmartProtocol\HttpListener and \SugarCraft\GitServer\Support\WorkerFork) — and the git:// and SSH transports remain on the shared-loop design described here.
shutdown(): voidRequest graceful shutdown. In sync mode the main loop observes the flag on its next select timeout; in async mode teardown is scheduled on the loop immediately.
listenAddress(): ?stringActual bound address in async mode (useful when the configured port is 0 = ephemeral). Null when not listening asynchronously.
config(): Config
repos(): array
isRunning(): bool
activeConnections(): int
subscriptions(): Subscriptions

AuthAttemptBudget final class

File-backed token budget for HTTP Basic authentication attempts (finding 008).

MethodSummary

charge(string $peer, string $username): ?intCharge one authentication attempt against the peer AND username buckets. AuthBudgetExhausted final class

Control-flow signal that the AuthAttemptBudget refused an authentication attempt before any bcrypt work was paid for. It is caught by Server::handleRequest() and answered 429 + Retry-After; it never denotes a server fault, so it must never reach the 500 path.

HttpListener final class

The socket half of smart HTTP: accepts TCP connections, buffers complete HTTP/1.1 requests (Content-Length or chunked bodies — git's own client POSTs its negotiation chunked), hands them to the synchronous router Server::handleRequest(), and writes the buffered response back in full — a bounded drain that keeps feeding a non-blocking socket until the kernel window empties repeatedly or the client stalls — before closing. One request per connection: every response carries Connection: close, matching the router's own header.

MethodSummary

start(): voidBind and start accepting. Port 0 asks the kernel for an ephemeral one — read it back through listenAddress(). Throws on bind failure (fail-fast; a half-listening server is the scaffold sin this listener exists to keep out).
stop(): voidStop accepting, drop the watches, end every worker, and drop every client; idempotent.

SugarCraft\GitServer\Support

AtomicWriter final class

The library's single atomic-write discipline (042): content lands on an exclusive temp inode in the TARGET DIRECTORY, gets its mode settled before payload bytes, is fsynced, and only then is renamed over the destination. A crash or a full disk can therefore only ever leave the OLD bytes or the orphaned temp visible — never a truncated file that silently un-publishes a visibility marker or zeroes a config.

MethodSummary
static write(string $path, string $contents, int $mode = 0600): voidPublish $contents at $path atomically.
static ensureDir(string $path, int $mode): voidCreate (or mode-settle) a directory with an EXPLICIT mode — mkdir's mode argument is umask-eroded, so the chmod after creation is what actually makes the requested bits true (038: the init jail must not land 0755 on a permissive-umask box).
static sweepStaleTemps(string $dir, int $olderThanSeconds = self::STALE_TEMP_AGE_SECONDS, int $maxDepth = 0): intSweep stray temps we minted (107): files matching our temp signature whose mtime is older than $olderThanSeconds and whose owner is the running user. $maxDepth > 0 descends subdirectories (the LFS shard tree) but only through plain directories, and the walk is capped — it is a hygiene sweep, not a catalogue.

Synchronous argv-only subprocess runner with a hard deadline.

MethodSummary
static reapPending(): intCollect any parked children that have exited since. Returns the number reaped; public so a test (or a shutdown path) can force a sweep without fabricating another spawn.
static pendingCount(): intNumber of handles parked awaiting a non-blocking reap.
static run(array $argv, float $timeoutSeconds = self::DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, array $extraEnv = [], ?int $maxOutputBytes = null): arrayLine-oriented contract (the historical shape every metadata parser here depends on): stdout split into lines, stderr merged in on failure only.
static runRaw(array $argv, float $timeoutSeconds = self::DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, array $extraEnv = [], ?int $maxOutputBytes = null): arrayByte-exact contract (S16, finding 031): stdout arrives as written, no line-split and no implode — a CRLF file round-trips as CRLF. Callers serving blob content use this so the bytes they hand out are the repository's bytes.

HttpWire final class

Shared HTTP transport primitives for the lib's two socket faces.

MethodSummary
static writeAll($stream, string $bytes, ?float $stallSeconds = null, ?float $absoluteSeconds = null): intPush $bytes through a non-blocking stream, retrying every partial accept until the whole payload is handed to the kernel — or until the client makes zero progress for $stallSeconds, or the write outlives the absolute ceiling, or the socket errors. Returns the byte count actually written (== strlen($bytes) on success); the caller's close path is identical either way because a half-delivered response is already protocol-dead to the client.

LogSafety final class

The lib's single client-token neutralizer for the operator log (027).

MethodSummary
static token(string $token): stringNeutralize a client-claimed token for the operator log. The token arrives straight from the peer: a CR/LF inside it forges additional STDERR lines, and an unbounded one floods the log. Strip C0 controls and DEL, collapse whitespace runs, and clip. Identity on any legitimate name — lookups and dispatch still run on the RAW token, so sanitizing here cannot alias a real account or rewrite which route was served.

Version final class

Reads the version stamped into a running phar archive's metadata.

MethodSummary
static resolve(string $archive, string $fallback): stringResolve the version for the current run.
static fromPharMetadata(string $archivePath): ?stringRead and normalize the version stamp inside an archive, or null when the path is empty, is not a file, is not a readable phar, or its stamp is neither a comparable X.Y.Z release nor a canonical commit-naming dev-<hex> build stamp. Every failure mode falls back to null rather than throwing — a corrupt archive must not crash --version.
static isDev(string $version): boolWhether $version names a DEV build: its lowercase spelling starts with DEV_PREFIX. Deliberately the literal rule and nothing more (mirror of candy-code's isDev) — dev-master classifies as dev, and self::displayLabel() simply has no commit to render from it because fromPharMetadata() never surfaces one.
static displayLabel(string $archive, string $fallback): stringThe string --version prints (053): a comparable release — or any run outside an archive, or one whose stamp names nothing readable — answers exactly as self::resolve() does; a dev build carries its commit as a parenthetical over the compiled-in base triple, 0.1.0 (dev-abc1234), so the output names BOTH the product's train and the exact build. The phar-latest smoke gate greps for the raw dev-<sha> substring, which is why the stamp travels verbatim inside the label.

WorkerFork final class

Fork-per-request worker pool — owner ruling 8b (G-5/G-1 wave).

MethodSummary
__construct(private readonly int $maxWorkers = self::DEFAULT_MAX_WORKERS, private readonly float $ceilingSeconds = self::DEFAULT_CEILING_SECONDS)
static supported(): bool
fork(callable $handler, $client, array $foreign = []): boolSpawn a worker owning $client. $foreign are the parent's other live descriptors (listener socket, other clients) which the child closes IMMEDIATELY so a wedged-or-alive worker can never hold a port or another client's stream open. $handler is a blocking pump: called repeatedly in the child, returns false when the connection is done.
reap(): intNon-blocking collect of every worker that has exited. Returns the count reaped; each reap also closes that worker's death-pipe end, which is what lets a live worker see EOF if the parent stops the pool.
live(): intLive workers right now (sweeps first).
terminateAll(): voidOrderly end for every worker: TERM, bounded poll, KILL the stragglers. Idempotent; safe on an empty pool.
peakCount(): intMaximum simultaneous workers any run of this pool has held.
totalSpawned(): intTotal workers this pool has ever spawned.
